chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The reversion (raj'ah) is the copulation, or else, it is only one (divorce).

key_terms.الْجِمَاعُ: Copulation/Intercourse: The physical act of sexual union, here defined as the substantive requirement for reversion.
key_terms.الْمُرَاجَعَةُ: Reversion (Raj'ah): The act of revoking a revocable divorce and returning the wife to the marital state without a new contract.
key_terms.وَاحِدَةٌ: One: Referring to a single (one) revocable divorce (taliq), as opposed to a final or double divorce.

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a valid revocation of divorce (raj'ah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the jurisprudential consensus that physical consummation is the definitive condition for revoking a revocable divorce (raj'ah), distinguishing it from mere verbal intent. It underscores the practical implication that without sexual intercourse, the divorce status remains unchanged, preserving the wife's rights during the waiting period (iddah). This ruling is central to Shia fiqh regarding the mechanics of talaq and the restoration of marital bonds.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The reversion, it is the copulation, or else, rather it is one (divorce)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated, from his father from ibn abu Nasr from ‘Abd al-Karim from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Going back to one’s wife is to go to bed with her, otherwise, it is counted as one divorce.”’
